ground_truth_note: The claim that cooked rice must be thrown out after 24 hours is inaccurate. According to the USDA and food safety experts, cooked rice is safe to eat for 3 to 4 days if it is refrigerated promptly and stored properly. http://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety
note_text: Cooked rice lasts 3-4 days refrigerated, not 24 hours. The 24-hour rule applies to room-temperature rice, which is unsafe after 2 hours due to bacterial growth. https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/does-rice-go-bad

logs.search.results:
**No, you do not have to throw out rice after 24 hours.** Cooked rice safely lasts **3-6 days** in the refrigerator when stored properly in an airtight container and cooled quickly after cooking, according to food safety guidelines from multiple sources[1][2][3].

**Supporting details from sources contradicting the 24-hour claim:**
- Healthline states cooked rice keeps for **3-4 days** (some sources say up to a week) in the fridge or **8 months** frozen, with risks only from improper storage allowing bacterial growth like Bacillus cereus[2] (https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/does-rice-go-bad).
- Chicoricerice.com specifies cooked brown rice lasts **4-6 days** refrigerated or **6 months** frozen, emphasizing quick cooling and airtight storage to prevent bacteria[1] (https://www.chicorice.com/blogs/all-about-rice/how-to-store-brown-rice).
- Mill.com aligns with USDA recommendations of **3-4 days** in the fridge for cooked rice (or **8 months** frozen), noting refrigeration slows but doesn't stop bacterial growth—discard if it smells off, feels gooey, or shows mold[3] (https://www.mill.com/blog/does-rice-expire).

No credible sources support discarding rice after exactly 24 hours; the claim likely stems from confusion with room-temperature rice (unsafe after 2 hours due to bacterial risks) or overly cautious advice. Always reheat to 165°F/74°C.
